text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"Applying the consolidation technique (periodic summarization of accumulated context) described in the arXiv paper to the naive‑append baseline will reduce cross‑fact interference, shrink token growth, and narrow the ~9 F1 point performance gap with the rewrite operation observed in the ablation study.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["f9710547","13b3b6fa"],"tags":["consolidation","token_budget","ablation","rewrite","naive_append"]},{"statement":"The day‑20 token‑budget overflow seen with naive‑append corresponds to the predicted onset of cross‑fact interference described in the consolidation paper, suggesting that the 20‑day horizon is a measurable marker of interference accumulation in long‑running simulations.","confidence":0.62,"support_ids":["f9710547","13b3b6fa"],"tags":["interference","temporal_dynamics","token_budget","simulation"]}]}
